strategy.summary: Reproduce the Cauchy distribution accuracy bug in scipy.stats: on the buggy revision cauchy.ppf(0.5) is -6.123233995736766e-17 (tan(pi*q - pi/2) with inexact pi/2), so the new TestCauchy ppf/isf cases with ref 0.0 at p=0.50 and the cdf/sf tail cases fail; on the fixed revision (Boost-wrapped scu._cauchy_ppf/_cauchy_isf and arctan2-based cdf/sf) they pass. Build scipy from the buggy commit 87ed0cab1a60 and run the two added tests in scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py.

system_packages: C++ compiler with C++11 support (Boost headers are bundled as needed by scipy special)
pinned_because: numpy: no documented constraint in the evidence; pick a numpy compatible with the buggy commit's build requirements (the era-inferred choice, not documented), and say so when reporting results

scipy special Boost wrapping: no documented constraint; the buggy commit must be built from source because scu._cauchy_ppf does not exist there in the form the fix expects, so the build must be of the buggy tree itself

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py::TestCauchy::test_ppf_isf (parametrized, including p=0.50 ref=0.0) and TestCauchy::test_cdf_sf (tail points x=-5e15 and x=5e15)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 87ed0cab1a60, TestCauchy::test_ppf_isf[0.50-ref0.0-...] fails because assert_allclose(x, 0.0, rtol=1e-15) sees about -6.12e-17 (a relative-tolerance check against zero reduces to near-exact equality), and the tail cdf/sf cases with rtol=1e-15 fail as well; on the fixed revision the whole TestCauchy class passes and the cauchy entry in fails_cmplx does not cause a failure in test_continuous_basic.py.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import scipy.stats as s; print(repr(s.cauchy.ppf(0.5)))" (buggy: -6.123233995736766e-17; fixed: 0.0)
risks: The buggy-revision failure depends on the build: the tan-based expression is deterministic in IEEE double, but results can differ across libm/numpy builds, so confirm the -6.12e-17 value before trusting the transition.

The evidence does not state a magnitude threshold; the tail tests rely on rtol=1e-15 at x=5e15, which may be sensitive to platform libm and may fail on the buggy revision for reasons other than the core ppf(0.5) defect.
Subnormal inputs (5e-324) and overflow to -inf for small p are mentioned but not established as part of the test transition; do not rely on them.
The buggy commit hash and PR date were not confirmed by the passages; verify that 87ed0cab1a60 is the pre-fix parent of PR 21335.
The fix uses Boost-wrapped functions; the bug is not expected to show on a non-standard architecture or sanitiser build, and a build with a different BLAS or compiler could mask or shift it.
numpy version is unbounded in the evidence; the choice of numpy version is an era-inferred decision and not documented.

oracle.tolerance: rtol=1e-15 in the added tests (as written by the developer)
oracle.reference_source: mpmath reference values in the added test_distributions.py TestCauchy class
oracle.why: The developer's test uses assert_allclose with rtol=1e-15 against mpmath references; this is the oracle used for the transition.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision cauchy.ppf(0.5) returns -6.123233995736766e-17; assert_allclose against reference 0.0 with rtol=1e-15 fails because the relative tolerance against zero is effectively exact equality, and the tail cdf/sf checks also exceed rtol=1e-15.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision ppf(0.5) returns exactly 0.0 via scu._cauchy_ppf and the cdf/sf arctan2 forms meet rtol=1e-15, so TestCauchy passes and test_continuous_basic cauchy handling is consistent with the fails_cmplx change.
